title: GenAI Evaluation & Ops
blurb: Diagnose the failure, then pick the intervention that fits it.
source: AWS Certified AI Practitioner (AIF-C01) exam guide · Domain 3
hint: Drag each situation onto the response it calls for. Some responses on the board are there to tempt you.

items.label: Answers read well but include claims absent from the retrieved policy passages.
items.why: First determine whether claims are supported, then tighten evidence use, refusal behavior, and citation validation. Trade-off: A larger model may improve fluency without solving missing or ignored evidence.

items.label: The answer generator cannot use the right fact because the relevant passage is absent from the retrieved set.
items.why: Retrieval recall isolates whether chunking, embeddings, filters, query rewriting, or candidate count misses needed evidence. Trade-off: Generation changes cannot recover evidence that never enters the context.

items.label: The relevant passage is present, but it is buried among many distracting chunks.
items.why: Better filters, hybrid retrieval, and reranking reduce noise while preserving the best evidence. Trade-off: Increasing candidate count can improve recall but may worsen precision, latency, and token cost.

items.label: A prompt change improved test examples but degraded several important customer workflows.
items.why: A versioned representative evaluation set detects regressions across use cases before release. Trade-off: Human review remains valuable when guided by a rubric and sampled across the real distribution.

items.label: An LLM judge consistently scores longer answers higher even when concise answers are correct.
items.why: LLM judges can have position, verbosity, and self-preference biases and must be calibrated with human judgments. Trade-off: Automated judging remains useful for scale after its rubric and bias are validated.

items.label: Usage is steady, but average input context and output length have tripled.
options: Track Tokens, Trim Context, and Cap Output
items.answer: Track Tokens, Trim Context, and Cap Output
items.why: Token telemetry exposes the direct cost driver; retrieve less noise, summarize history, cache stable context, and cap output. Trade-off: Provisioned throughput helps predictable high utilization, not wasteful prompt growth by itself.

items.label: Many users ask semantically equivalent questions about unchanged public information.
items.why: A carefully keyed cache can reduce latency and token spend for equivalent requests when freshness and access boundaries are respected. Trade-off: Do not cache sensitive, personalized, rapidly changing, or insufficiently isolated responses.

items.label: A support agent calls the same failing API until its execution budget is exhausted.
options: Add Call Limits, Error State, and Fallback
items.answer: Add Call Limits, Error State, and Fallback
items.why: Bounded retries, explicit error handling, idempotency, observability, and human escalation prevent runaway loops. Trade-off: Improving tool descriptions helps selection but does not replace runtime limits and failure controls.

items.label: A medical support model is uncertain and the cost of a wrong recommendation is severe.
options: Abstain and Route to Human Review
items.answer: Abstain and Route to Human Review
items.why: Confidence thresholds, abstention, evidence display, and qualified human review are appropriate for consequential uncertainty. Trade-off: Human oversight needs clear responsibility, useful context, and measured review quality rather than ceremonial approval.
